campaign.name: The Sunken Citadel
campaign.description: A short pitch for the whole campaign — setting, tone, the party's starting situation.

encyclopediaEntries.title: Port Vessa
encyclopediaEntries.body:
A smugglers' port town built into a sea cliff — half the buildings are condemned, and the other half don't ask questions.

What the party notices first: the harbor smells like tar and low tide, and every conversation stops when a stranger walks in.

Hook: the harbormaster is three months behind on payments to whoever actually runs the docks.

encyclopediaEntries.title: Harbormaster Ilsevet Cray
encyclopediaEntries.body:
Runs the port's paperwork, owes the wrong people money, and will absolutely sell out the party if it clears her debt.

Wants: to leave town quietly, ideally with the ledger nobody knows she copied.

Secret: that ledger names every smuggler crew working the coast — including the one she reports to.

encyclopediaEntries.title: The Undertow
encyclopediaEntries.body:
A loose network of smugglers moving contraband along the coast — less an organization than a shared understanding not to rat each other out.

Leadership: nobody claims to be in charge, which is the point.

Reach: every port town within three days' sail has at least one Undertow contact.

bestiaryEntries.name: Cliffside Ghoul
bestiaryEntries.traits: Keen Smell. Has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.
bestiaryEntries.actions: Claw. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 2d6+3 slashing damage.
bestiaryEntries.notes: Lairs in the sea caves below Port Vessa — good early "why is this town scared" reveal.

notes.title: Session zero — hooks and secrets
notes.body:
What the party doesn't know yet: who the harbormaster really owes, and that the ledger she copied names every Undertow contact on the coast.

Opening hook: the party arrives in Port Vessa needing passage, and the harbormaster is the only one who can arrange it — for a price.
